title: Five Belts Around the Globe
question: Why is Earth divided into tropical, temperate and frigid zones?
hook: In the tropics the Sun passes straight overhead twice a year, yet in the temperate zones it never does even once.
idea: How high the Sun climbs at each latitude splits Earth into the Torrid Zone, two temperate zones and two frigid zones, each with its own pattern of light and seasons.

beats.prompt: Follow the overhead Sun through the year, starting at the June solstice.
items: Overhead at the Tropic of Cancer
Moving south over the northern tropics
Overhead at the Tropic of Capricorn
beats.explain: The overhead Sun reaches the Tropic of Cancer at the June solstice, heads south past the September equinox, reaches the Tropic of Capricorn at the December solstice, and returns to the equator for the March equinox.

beats.prompt: Match each part of the globe to what it experiences.
pairs: The Sun can pass straight overhead
Six months of day, six of night
beats.explain: The Sun's height sets each zone's pattern: overhead in the tropics, never overhead in the mild belts, and long days and nights near the poles.

beats.prompt: A town sits right on the edge of a frigid zone, on the Arctic Circle. What happens there on the winter solstice?

choices.label: The Sun does not rise all day
The Sun stays up for 24 hours
choices.feedback: That happens on the summer solstice, the opposite day of the year.

choices.label: The Sun passes straight overhead at noon
choices.feedback: The Sun is only ever directly overhead within the tropics.

beats.explain: At the edge of a frigid zone there is one day, the winter solstice, when the Sun is too low to rise, and one day at the summer solstice when it never sets.

beats.prompt: One step in this ancient reasoning is wrong; which?
steps: The region around the equator was thought too hot for living
The region from the Arctic Circle to the pole was thought permanently frozen
The temperate zone between them was thought habitable
So people could live only in the temperate zone
beats.explain: Humans have in fact lived in almost all of Earth's climates, including inside the Arctic Circle.
